text_fidelity_a: Zoom Hydraulic Disc Brakes Mountain Bike Sets MTB Front & Rear Set with Floating Disc Rotor 160mm & Color Bolts (Gold) These brakes were decent until i decided to internally route the rear hose and shorten it a bit.  After trying for many hours to remove the hose from the lever, so I could route my hose internally, I decided to try removing the hose from the caliper end. The connecting nut was so tight, it wouldn't budge. I know how tight they are supposed to be, and this was tight far beyond specs. Almost as if they were never meant to come apart at all. So I took the bike to my local bike shop. After a half hour of trying to remove the hose, they told me there's a risk of breaking something,  land they aren't able to do it because they don't want to be responsible if something breaks. The connecting nut on the lever was far too tight as well. But I was able to break it loose in the beginning. But i was not able to remove the hose, probably because the olive was so deformed from the overtightened nut to begin with. And the nut on the caliper end won't budge at all. So basically, im stuck with a 1 piece break set. Nothing will come apart, because the factory overtightened everything so tight, its impossible to take apart without breaking something.  Im forced to take this 70$ loss, but I do not recommend these brakes if u have  any intentions of ever needing to take them apart for whatever reason. I don't see other reviews with this problem,  so its possible I have an error set, and they aren't all like this. But from a personal perspective, my experience is 100% dissatisfaction.  I'm beyond the return time frame. Lesson learned. Sometimes, even the good reviews can lead to a bad purchase. Unfortunately, I am ordering Shimano like my gut told me to from the beginning.  I'm not weak man, and am Very familiar with all components of a mountain bike,  and whoever or whatever tightened these nuts on both ends of the brake line went WELL BEYOND tight. U may as well have welded them.
text_fidelity_b: Zoom Hydraulic Disc Brakes Mountain Bike Sets MTB Front & Rear Set with Floating Disc Rotor 160mm & Color Bolts (Gold)

The body is plastic, but it's a good quality plastic that has a nice, solid feel to it. The army green housing is nicely complemented with a bamboo surround on the base. The rope handle is functional and attractive. The cage and hanging points are metal. The USB charge port has a silicone cap to keep water/dirt out. The cap is tethered to the body so it won't get lost.

Controls are simple: a single knob that turns it on with a nice, solid click. It has a good dimmable range, from a soft night light level to a full room (or tent) level of light.

The best feature is that it uses standard 18650 Li-ion batteries. I am so tired of battery powered items that have non-removable batteries since, when the battery eventually fails, you have to toss the item. With this, you just have to replace the 18650 cells when they will no longer hold a charge well. Plus, since I always have charged 18650 cells for other items, when the batteries run down I don't have to wait for the lantern to charge -- just swap out the batteries for a freshly charged set and you're back in business.

The batteries can be charged without having to remove them (there's a USB C port on the lantern body with a single LED charge light indicator) but, as with any 18650, it's best to charge them in an external charger. The cells claim to be 2400 mAh, but that's somewhat optimistic -- I get a bit less than 2000 mAh capacity when I discharged and metered them. The internal charge rate is 0.6A -- a bit slow, but ideal for good battery longevity.

My only quibble is that I would have liked if the included batteries were from a major brand, such as Sony/Murata, Samsung or LG. But the ones included have been performing fine since an LED light is a pretty low-demand task for an 18650 cell.

A good performing, good looking light that you won't have to toss when the batteries reach their end of life. Five stars and a good value for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Tresda Camping Lantern Rechargeable, 370LM Dimmable LED Vintage Battery Powered Lanterns, Waterproof LED Retro Camping Lights for Camping, Power Outages, Hurricane, Outdoors, Home Décor

text_fidelity_a:
Thule SUP Taxi XT Surfboard Rack This is just fantastic quality and design, as I've come to expect from Thule. Seems that you just can't find a better product. And in this case, I'm not sure anyone else makes carriers specifically for stand up paddleboards. It has a smooth and super slick width adjusting system, and it adjusts so much that you can pile two boards in this setup with a divider between them for protection.

It seems there is a thin, steel braided cable inside the strap to deter casual thieves (although I could cut it with a good diagonal cutters, which is probably something I could find in my trunk, but perhaps only because I like tools). Anyway, I think that and the included locking cylinders make this about the most secure setup that you can get.

Speaking of the locking cylinders, they use the same type of keys as my other Thule stuff. But you'll have to special order them separately if you want to have on key for all your gear. I don't know of any program to make this easier on you, but it would be great if they just gave you a voucher for new locking cylinders if you have already registered one of their other products or something like that. I'm actually not certain if you can remove them once you put them in...

The only thing I don't like is the nylon rope to hold the front of the boards down. I mean, I just don't like having to use this cumbersome and annoying, old-style method, but this is just inherent to hauling boards and there's really nothing Thule can do about it (although you never know what they'll come up with). This is just a physics problem that hasn't been completely solved.

Yeah, the materials are perfect, the design is well-thought out and specific. You just really can't beat this thing. It is impressive in its own right. It's for sure on the top end of what I want to pay, but it is nice to have the best.
text_fidelity_b: Thule SUP Taxi XT Surfboard Rack

TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system The physical therapist at the hospital had me work on hers when I came in. She thinks the TRX system is the bee's knees. When the thearopy was over I bought one.

Importantly note that the physical therapist specifically told me not to get a knock off unless it had a single strap. If the straps were not connected I would lose the balance building part and she said it would hurt me more than help. The TRX was the only one I saw, at the time, that met her criteria.

I love working on it. In my opinion, There are a couple of things to consider. First is that at my age and inflexibility, the lower body work outs are difficult. You have to get your feet in the straps a certain way and sometimes I find it hard to keep the feet in and do the workout.

The next consideration is that it is difficult to use in a closed door. You really need a fair amount of space around you to work out, and I find a closed door is a hindrance.

Overall i must grudgingly admit the physical therapist is right and the TRX system is just about perfect for getting that resistance training which is so important.
text_fidelity_b: TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system

Viwki Pocket Folding Knife with 3.34" Blade for Hunting Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC,Handle w/Embossed Flag, Liner Lock, Flipper Open,Deep Carry Pocketclip [[VIDEOID:9da43d167e588a5ad01ee0a38d9abd08]] First of all, I have a lot of knives. From cheap ones to expensive ones. I always take them apart when I first get them and clean them, add oil where needed and inspect.

At this price, the action on this knife is amazing (see video). While the listing says ceramic bearings these are steel bearings for the pivot (see photos). It is still extremely smooth for deploy and for closing (even though it uses the tiny caged bearings, and they sit directly on the tang without grooves for said caged bearings).

The g10 is nicely textured with just enough checkering, and they are very slim scales which I appreciate as it is a bit bigger for a folder lengthwise. The slim scales give it a great feel and it really is very nice on the pocket and not as noticeable as other knives this length. The clip isn't ambidextrous however (but is tip up) and is right hand carry. It also isn't a deep carry clip but it works well enough (and there are many clips that would work with this 3-screw setup for the pocket clip).

I'm normally not a huge fan of tanto blade shapes but this has the tip grind elongated so that angle on this is much more usable, and looks better in my opinion. It could benefit from some jimping on the spine also, but this is minor.

The lockup is solid, with no wiggle even when getting the blade and pivot to a point where it drops shut.

Really a nice knife overall (and I can sometimes be critical with knives, specifically cheaper knives). At this price point it is really a great value and I'm glad to have received!
text_fidelity_b: Viwki Pocket Folding Knife with 3.34" Blade for Hunting Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC,Handle w/Embossed Flag, Liner Lock, Flipper Open,Deep Carry Pocketclip

Coleman 3000000455 Latern Pump Kit This kit is dog easy the second time around. Unfortunately the second time may be decades away. Hopefully.
I faithfully disassembled my pump from my 45 year old Coleman stove (Bless em! Most of the guys who built the thing are no doubt long gone to their various rewards)....but anyway, I elected to rebuild the old pump which was a mistake. The new cup is designed for the new rod. It does not work on the old one.
On the old rod there is a metal stop that holds the cup. The new cup is different. If you have a super oldie like mine you will take the metal retaining clip off the new pump with needle nosed pliars. Wiggle under the metal clip and wiggle it off. Slide everything off. Put the round metal ring thingy which holds it to the tank on, then the spring. Follow with the NYLON stop ring. Then put the cup on top of that followed by the new round metal spring clip, or the old. That much is the same.
Put it back in the unit. I started it at the bottom and chased it around with my thumbnail until all of the cup was in....then shoved it home. Some people might have elected to put a bit of grease on the cup before installation but I chose the venerable 3-1 oil before...and after.
After all that it worked like a charm. It's quick and simple if you do it right.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman 3000000455 Latern Pump Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue After Hurricane Sandy hit the east coast and I was without power for 9 days, I decided to purchase one more light to add to my army of 13 flashlights. I wanted something that would illuminate a room better than my underwater flashlight and my headlamp. My underwater flashlight and head lamp happen to be exceptional lights but they can only be used for focused tasks since they lack a wide range. This lantern not only gives exceptional light but it also illuminates an entire small room.

These are the many features I like:

- The lantern is so bright it is blinding but it definitely lights up my kitchen from 1/2 a room away. I just had to make sure I did not look the light in the eye.
- It has a high and low mode.
- It can also be used as a strobe light (meaning in blinking mode).
- It only takes only 3 D size batteries (only one more battery than most D-battery flashlights).
- It's water resistant.
- It comes with a lifetime warranty.
- The lantern has a tent hook on the bottom; although it is a bit difficult to move.
- It also has an EZ-find light that blinks every few seconds; although that "find" light (which sits above the black power button) is barely visible in the dark.
- Customer service is excellent.

The only problem I had with this light is that it did not come with any instructions; it only comes with a wrap-around paper touting its virtues. Therefore, I had to call the company on the 800 I found on the Internet (you can find that # in my comments) to learn how to make the strobe light work. I also asked how the EZ find light worked because I was unable to detect it.

The tent hook and handle are self-explanatory but to make this light work, this is what I had to do. Please note I executed all these instructions with the front of the lantern facing me:

1. Both the top and bottom of the lantern screw off. The top is where the blub is and that can be screwed off counter-clockwise but there's really no reason to remove the top. I screwed off the bottom clockwise and inserted the 3 D batteries as indicated on the stickers inside. I then lined up the red arrows (both on lid and case) when closing the bottom in the opposite direction I opened it and made I heard it click shut.

2. I pushed the black button to operate the light. Pressing it once brought on high mode and pressing it again brought on low mode. Sometimes I found that after one press no light comes on; in that case I pressed it again until I was in the desired mode. The tech said this was normal behavior.

3. To get the strobe light working, I had to HOLD down the black button for about 5 or 6 seconds until the light started to flash. I then pressed the black button to turn the strobe effect off.

4. To see the EZ find light that is located above the black on off button, I moved the lantern to a totally dark room. This light flashed every 5 or 6 seconds but I still found it hard to see.

In summary, this is a great lantern for illuminating a small room or anywhere I need to illuminate a larger area than a flashlight can provide. The light given off seems fluorescent but it's bright enough to work with. The only thing I did not like is that instructions on how to operate the strobe, insert the batteries, etc. were not provided. Although I was able to figure out how to do most of this, I had no clue I had to HOLD down the on/off button for 5 or 6 seconds to get the strobe feature to work. Since this lantern is going into storage until I need it, I will take out the batteries as the EZ find light will probably drain them after a couple of months.
text_fidelity_b: Rayovac SE3DLNBL Sportsman 240 Lumen 3D LED Lantern, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
SUBOOS Compact 3-in-1 Rechargeable LED Camping Lantern and Flashlight - 290 Lumens, Waterproof, Great for Suvival Kit, Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage. We sometimes have seasons of power outages where I live. That is not a problem sometimes, but if it is a long extended one, it is handy to have lights available to use so we can continue life as normal as much as possible, especially in unlit areas like bathroom and basement. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This light is quite compact, yet large enough to stand up on the table. It has a hanging wire on the top of it that folds down. There is a round cloudy covering on the bottom, and a clear reflective opening on the top for the flashlight. There are curved textured see through coverings which are for red lights either constant or flashing.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is really quite handy. A quick press will turn on the basic light. Another press, medium. Another press, high. One more press. Off. The light is pretty easy to see with and makes a great light if you have to work hands free at a table, or near metal surface which it will magnetically stick to.

FLASHLIGHT
The flashlight has two rapid presses and then one more will turn it brighter then off.

RED LIGHT
If you need to use a red light or need to attract attention you can use the red light consistent or flashing.

BOOKLET
The booklet in the package is well written and has great instructions how to use this.

CHARGING
The charging cord is USB to mini USB cord. There are five blue lights on the side and they will light up as the light is charged. When done, they stay lit until you unplug it.

LONGEVITY
We got several hours out of this on medium and high and it still has half a charge. It charges up pretty quickly in only a couple of hours, and you can use this with a power bank if you need to.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This magnetized light can either stand up on a table, stick to a metal surface, or hang by the wire from a string, hook, etc. It is plenty bright enough to use for emergencies or camping and lasts quite a few hours prior to having to charge again.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great light to have handy, but over time, if anything changes, I will update. For now, it is performing well and lasts a good amount of time prior to needing a recharge.
text_fidelity_b: SUBOOS Compact 3-in-1 Rechargeable LED Camping Lantern and Flashlight - 290 Lumens, Waterproof, Great for Suvival Kit, Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage.

Any rope will do in a pinch, but it’s much better when you have a fancy rope made for the purpose and a rope that easily goes the extra mile is this Smart Jump Rope.

What do you get with this jump rope? You get a rope that has electronic controls that tell you how many turns you make, how many minutes you jump, and the total calories burned. One of the interesting options with this jump rope is that you can perform the action without using the actual rope. This cordless option might sound unusual at first, but the idea is to jump off the ground with each turn of your wrists. You are still getting the same fitness as with a rope, without the annoyance of not clearing the rope with your feet and possibly getting tangled or tripping.

Once you finish using this digital jumping rope just pack it up in the included storage bag until your next scheduled exercise time. If you’re a fitness freak who likes precise, scientific measurements, your next exercise time will likely be sooner than you think. I can’t speak for everyone, but I like anything that shows my statistics, and I am motivated to exercise more when I can see the facts like number of turns, total minutes, and calories burned.

We could all use a little more exercise in our daily routine. This digital jump rope is an excellent way to better fitness and it’s the only jump rope I have ever used with digital readouts. Get one for yourself and improve your health.

My Sierra Designs tent could be fully assembled in less than 60 seconds and broken down and packed away in about 2 minutes even in the most unfavorable conditions. This tent took me over 5 minutes to assemble in pristine conditions. May not sound like a lot but when you need a tent setup ASAP, the difference between having shelter in under a minute versus 5 or more minutes makes a big difference. The sticks are cheap and pale in comparison to the carbon fiber Easton sticks you get with Sierra Designs. It also is vulnerable to bugs. I was using this in an area that had a large ant population and ants kept finding their way into the tent somehow, even though the tent was completely zipped up. Never had this problem with my old tent.

For the money, it's not horrible. I'll definitely be replacing my old tent though and keeping this only as a backup.

LuxFit Ball Chair, Premium Fitness Exercise Ball Chairs for Home and Office 2 Year Warranty! with 2000lbs Static Strength Ball Great Office Desk Chair, and Stability Ball Chair I have been using this chair for a few weeks at my desk at work. I like it. As someone who is fairly fit and does an hour of ab work most weeks, I honestly can't say that I notice a drastic difference in my ab toning or how my abs feel after using this chair for hours a day. The difference I can notice is in my posture. My back used to hurt so much because I got in the bad habit of crossing my legs and leaning to one side, one forearm bracing my body using one arm of an office chair. Ouch. I knew I had to eliminate a stable backrest and armrests to retrain my posture, and I wanted to challenge my seated body more than in a basic office chair.

All around, this is a great chair. I love the rolling feature. I followed a suggestion of another reviewed to inflate to about 12", wait a day, then inflate further. It worked. Fully inflated, the height is 23", which is what I needed. I am 5'4" but my computer screen is mounted high off of my desk. The backrest is almost useless at my height, to be honest. I would never sit so far back in the chair to have my back touch the rest. Sometimes if I have been seated for several hours, my upper back will begin to hurt out of strain, so I will lean far back for a few moments. Also, it is good to use to stretch if twisting. If I had known what I know now, I would have opened my search to models without backrests. Alas. This chair is fine.

Women: I wear dresses that hit 1-2" above my knee most days. I had no problem sitting on this chair. I work in an enclosed L-shape desk and I have spread my legs a little when sitting in this chair, but I haven't found it absolutely necessary or most comfortable. I can see how you gain great stability with widespread legs, but I'm most naturally inclined to have my legs straight in front of me. I can easily meet with someone seated across from me with my legs closed without feeling unstable. The one caveat to this is high heels-- I'm not talking about 1" wedges, but 2"+ and pointies-- it will be less sturdy to navigate and you may feel compelled to spread your legs to gain your balance.

Additional info from several months of use: You definitely expend more energy sitting on this bad boy. I came down with the flu and my first day back in office I sat down for a few moments and knew I wasn’t strong enough to stay in this chair.
text_fidelity_b: LuxFit Ball Chair, Premium Fitness Exercise Ball Chairs for Home and Office 2 Year Warranty! with 2000lbs Static Strength Ball Great Office Desk Chair, and Stability Ball Chair

This one has a learning curve, but the trade off is you are getting a very portable shade that is not only for beaches. This is the perfect shelter for hikers who want basic protection from the elements. One thing that I discovered is if you attempt to set this up without regard to prevailing wind (or even breeze) you could be chasing it. It's a big sail and it does not take much to catch it and lift it if you do not heed Lebryk's advice regarding angling the stakes when you secure it to the ground.

While it is not waterproof, it will keep you from getting drenched in the event it a fast rising storm. Again, this is of greater value to hikers, especially due to the light weight when this is in its carry bag.

For me the compactness is the biggest feature. After setting it up a few times you will level the learning curve. Folding and storing it properly will take a bit longer.

Now that I am accustomed to using this it is now part of my emergency 'bug out' kit - a collection of small, essential items that I can manage if I need to leave the area in a hurry. Since my locale can (and does) get hit with some scary weather from time to time, this one goes with me if I have to evacuate.

Whatever the reason you are considering this, I can assure you that if you take the limitations into account this is a bargain and very useful for a number of scenarios. Including the one for which it was designed: a portable cabana.
text_fidelity_b: Biga 2 Mesh Window, Outside Zipper Closure, Silver Coating, Portable Beach Quick Cabana/Shelter/Shade, Blue

King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.
text_fidelity_b: King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can Some Augason Farms stuff I buy as emergency food, some I buy for regular use. If I can price out something in this form that is same price or less than other forms, then I go with this as it can be stored away or kept in my working pantry. I use a lot of Augason Farms, and I've been pleased with this.

Dehydrated celery is a great addition to the pantry. Sometimes I dont have fresh, or I have fresh that went bad, or I dont find it in the store, or what is there looks bad, or price is way outside my budget. Having some dried celery tucked away in my pantry really helps stretch the budget and brings value to my time.

I keep the recipe trifecta on hand, "mire poix": celery, carrot, and onion. I keep fresh, frozen, and dried on hand. Usually used in recipes that will help rehydrate these foods no problem. Celery is very easy to rehydrate. I usually just add to the cooking process and its good to go.

Food scarcity is legit, so if you can stock up when items are on sale, then I recommend to do so. Consider it insurance.

FYI: food and such are sold based on weight, not volume. There is 1lb, 2 oz packed in this #10 can (that reads, "number ten" not "ten pound"- it is a size of can). Using a #10 can means that it provides uniformity among storage. Emergency supplies are packed for long term and are packed to stack. They also float. They can be repurposed. Even if one gets a dent, contents are still good (unless and actual hole, which is not likely to happen). The food will not be filled to the brim, and also.. food settles after packing.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Dehydrated Cross Cut Celery 1 lb 2 oz No. 10 Can

text_fidelity_a:
Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light I commute by bike and I'm obsessed with seeing and being seen at night. I have a 650 lumen TerraLUX TT-5 flashlight (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B009WFA4KU/) strapped to my handlebars as my primary light. I added this helmet-mounted light set as redundancy / extra security. I've had it about a month now.

This is a pretty good light. It's fairly bright, and I like that it has amber LED's on both sides of both the front and rear light. This makes you visible from any angle (hence the "360" in the name). Having gotten used to the blinding, virtual daylight of the 650 lumen flashlight on my handlebars, the 250 lumens that this light puts out on max doesn't seem quite bright enough to me. But I could get home safely with this alone if my flashlight were to fail, so it's bright enough.

Things I like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) You can aim the light wherever you need it. It's handy for checking out turns before you've made the turn. And I can now see the display from my bike computer without having to wait for a streetlight! And when I'm off my bike, I can see my lock, into my trunk bag, etc.
2) They increase visibility and therefore safety.
3) You'll probably leave them mounted to your helmet most of the time, so you're less likely to forget them. And if you're locking your bike up somewhere you'll probably take your helmet with you, so you'll automatically take your lights too - less chance of theft.

Things I like about this light in particular:
1) It's one of the brighter ones available.
2) It actively aims LED's in every direction, making you highly visible.
3) It's rechargeable and charges via USB.

Things I don't like about helmet-mounted lights in general:
1) They add weight to your head / neck.
2) They can get knocked around. I take my bike on the train for a portion of my commute, and when we near my stop I have my helmet on and am ready to get my bike out of the rack to disembark; meanwhile other riders are trying to get to their bikes. I frequently bang one or the other of the lights on the overhand above the bikes while we're all jostling around. Also, when I take my helmet off I feel I have to be more careful about stowing it so the lights don't get knocked about.

Things I don't like about this light in particular:
1) It's surprisingly heavy, and it's unbalanced. The front light is virtually weightless. The rear light, which has the battery pack, is surprisingly heavy. I invested in a very nice, "barely there" helmet that weighs virtually nothing. This light makes it feel like a brick. Obviously it's not that heavy, but it is heavier than I expected. And I don't like that all the weight is to the rear. This is okay when I'm leaning forward in riding position, but when I'm stopped at a light or otherwise upright, the weight is pulling my head back.
2) I find the rubberized button to turn it on / change modes difficult to feel and manipulate while I'm riding. If I don't take the train home, my commute is an hour and 15 minutes. To save battery I have it on low when I'm riding on well-lit streets and switch to high otherwise. I've had this light almost a month and I'm not getting better at feeling / adjusting the light. It takes concentration away from riding while I fiddle with it.
3) The tail light mode is not adjustable. It does this odd, slow fade-in / fade-out and that's it. You can't make it be always on, and you can't make it actually flash.
4) You can't have just the taillight on. Once the headlight's on, you can turn the taillight off independently, but you can't ride with just the taillight.
5) The battery is not replaceable. My flashlight / headlight runs on a replaceable, rechargeable battery, which means I can keep a spare battery in my pouch and be sure I have enough battery to get home. I can also ride with one battery while the other's at home recharging. With this light, if the battery runs out you can't use the light until you get to a USB charger. And it takes a good few hours to recharge, so you can't go riding for the hours it takes to recharge. And the low battery indicator is tucked away at the bottom of the taillight, and is only visible after you've plugged it in to recharge, so that doesn't help. So you'd better keep it charged.
6) You can change the angle of the front light, but only in discrete clicks. Each click is a very small angle of change on the device, but changes where the light hits the road by about 20'. I frequently want the light right in between two of the clicks and I can't put it there.
7) The helmet mounts strike me as odd. The front light slides into it's mount and clicks in place, but it slides in from the bottom. That means the if the clicky thing ever fails the light will slide out. If it slid in from the top gravity would keep it in place. And the rear light presses on with four tabs clicking into four slots. You really have to pull on it to dismount it. Odd.

Hmmm. Looking at this review there are way more things in the "don't like about this light" section than elsewhere, which makes it seem like I don't like this light. That's not true. None of the "don't likes" are show-stoppers. I'm keeping the light and I do like it. They're mostly just areas where I feel like the light could be somewhat better. If you buy this light you'll definitely be seen, you'll see where you're going, and you'll probably be happy you have it. These are just my observations for whatever they may be worth to you.
text_fidelity_b: Light & Motion Vis 360 Plus Bike Helmet Light

Kijaro Coast Portable Beach Breeze Hammock with Cup Holders and Pillow What a great hammock to bring to the beach. It's really comfortable, as comfortable as a hammock can be that is.
Has nice mesh so air flows underneath and laying on it doesn't get my back all hot and sweaty. I like the cup holders so I don't have to put my thermos glass into the sand.
What I really like to use this for is bathing my dogs. Because it hurts my back so much to bend over, we have one person sit on the hammock (going to get wet), and the other person, usually me, stand with the hose. We place the dog on the hammock and begin washing. The mesh allows the soap and water to run through, the hammock raises the dog up to a more reachable height and I'm sitting right there so it's not such a strain on my back.
My daughter in law is going to love this when they come down to visit us. She loves laying out and getting some sun while she's here in the south. As easy as this hammock is to open up and repack into the nice carry bag, she can get it up, do her sun tanning, then get it put back up when she's done.
I also like the convenience of this hammock. Can bring it out into the yard to relax under the shade of a tree on these hot summer days. Can bring it to our family picnics where a child can take a quick nap. Can bring to the beach and not have to worry about laying on the sand. Have it on our patio for bathing dogs or just for the kids to lay on while we're having our night time coffee out there.

Putting this together was really easy. The frame is already put together. I just had to fold it out then lock the pins into the frame. Now, stretching the mesh hammock onto the frame was a bit of a workout. It's very tight because it's new. The more times you put on and take off the hammock, the easier it will be to do so.
Well worth the money for the convenience and multiple uses of this hammock.

Both come incredibly sharp with the Skandinavian grind LOVE IT, but I do think I like the shorter, stouter blade of the Pro C better. They both have a rubberized texture so they will not get away from you. The old Companion "Clipper" had a plastic PVC handle. Ultimately, you can't go wrong with either one. They both have 2.0mm blades, and for certain bushcraft activities you may want a blade thats 2.5 to 3.5 mm thick, and both of these have models that come this thick- the Companion Heavy duty and the Robust.

I do think that the Companion came sharper than Pro C out of the box. I don't remember being able to shave the hair on my arm with it. However, I can now after sharpening and stropping it. Oh, the sheath on the Companion is considerably better. It holds the knife much more securely.

Edit: I do like the Pro-C better. The blade is a bit shorter and stouter and it changes the balance of the knife. For my purpose which is more of a general utility knife it's the better one. But they both get 5 stars from me.

text_fidelity_a:
Terrain D.O.G. Elevation Harness, Medium, 3/4" x 16"-25", Sky Blue/Silver/Purple Super, high quality harness with size adjustments on ALL straps. The buckles & clasps are all constructed of plastic, but still very durable. The material used for the harness looks to be thick nylon or composite. I might even say it's a little too stiff. But again, this speaks towards the quality of the product.

I had no issues getting it on our pup (Yorkie mix) & he didn't mind it at all.

The one caveat here is that that this is a REAR CLIP harness. If you (or your fur kid) is not used to a rear clip harness, then please be aware. Especially if he or she is used to a front or middle clip.

As with front or middle clip, your pup can be pulled back or away from a dangerous or unwanted situation. You can still do that with a rear clip, but he/she won't respond to the tug. So you won't be able to "steer" for lack of a better term. Basically, it would be like turning them butt first!

I believe the rear style clips are more suited for situations where your guy has a little more freedom to walk, jump or run, but you still want the harness in place. This way you can intervene & keep keep them from hurting themselves (IE: if he or she jumps, & the leash gets stuck, they are not hanging by their neck on the harness!)

So, In my opinion, not the best style harness for daily walks that require more control. However, if your needs are more for recreation or hiking or situations where you pup has more freedom, then this harness is a great solution.
text_fidelity_b: Terrain D.O.G. Elevation Harness, Medium, 3/4" x 16"-25", Sky Blue/Silver/Purple

text_fidelity_a:
M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube You see all of these reviews and they all start to sound the same, so I'll tell you where I'm coming from, my thoughts on the rod, and give my verdict.
I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube

I like the automatic True Ballistic Range calculation--it really lends itself well to hunting with rifle or bow. I also use this range finder's LOS settings for photography-related hobbies. Knowing distances of natural objects in a scene can help with prime lens choice, etc. This range finder is useful everywhere. In addition to being an awesome range finder, it makes for a great monocular. I find myself using it a lot while hunting rather than pulling up big, heavy binoculars. The magnification and clarity of the optic is great--which is to be expected from leupold.

I really like the case that came with the range finder. It carries the unit very well and it also has a card spot for carrying a range card. It actually includes a range card and a micro fiber cloth for cleaning your optics. Last but not least, the unit came with a battery. It is nice being able to take this out of the box and immediately use it. I bought [[ASIN:B0057ILX8S these batteries]] to use in it after the original is dead. The original that came with the unit is an energizer brand.

Dimensions of the case and the range finder unit can be seen in the photos I have uploaded

Included:

text_fidelity_a:
GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green Measuring 7'x5', the GT Global Beach Blanket is a nice size for a picnic lunch or to spread out on the beach for sunbathing. As others have previously noted, this "blanket" is a lightweight, thin, smooth nylon-like material with grommets around the sides, so it's more of a light tarp rather than a blanket, but that's not at all bad. This material stays cool to the touch so it would be a real relief to sunbathe on this rather than my towel which transfers heat directly to me when laying on it.

Sand doesn't stick to this material and water beads up and rolls right off it, so you could use this as a protective layer to keep your beach towels or blanket clean. Being very light, it's easy for the breeze to catch it and sail it away, so it has grommets strategically positioned around the sides which would allow it to be staked down. (Stakes not included). It could also make a handy sunshade if you had someplace to secure it from and some line.

It comes in a nylon carry case that's very tight so it's a bit of an effort to remove it. When you're done using it the bag would be handy to store it in again, but it's so tight that I was unable to place it back in. The manufacturer really needs to make the carry bag large enough that people could use it without struggling.

Even without going back into the bag though, this tarp folds and rolls up into a small bundle that would be easy to take along to the beach, waterpark, on camping trips, to stick in a backpack for trekking, or to stow on a boat. Besides using it for picnics or at the beach, this tarp would be very useful to have along when camping to provide a dry place to sit or to cover food stores or gear. Backpackers would find it useful to provide a safe dry seating area, to hang up by the grommets to get out of sudden downpours, and even as something to sleep on at night in a pinch. Boaters could find this tarp useful in many of the same ways and more, so this tarp has uses that go way beyond "beach blanket", and for those reasons I like it.

I'm giving it four stars rather than five because it's impossible to return the tarp to the carry bag once it's out of it, and it needs to come with stakes to hold it down in sand to be ready to use. Promotional discount received for evaluation and review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: GTGlobal Multifunctional Beach Blanket/ Picnic Mat with Carrying Pouch 7 X 5 Feet, Waterproof Tarp, Extra Large Perfect for Beach Party/ Outdoors/ Camping/ Hiking - Green

Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue I’m torn with how to rate this chair. I have the 360 swivel version ($60) as well as this one, which is about half the price. This compaclite chair has a higher back which makes it more comfortable than the swivel version, and the pillow actually is a nice plus. It’s compact and more comfortable than typical folding chairs. When compared to the swivel version, this one wins no contest. However, it still isn’t enough for it to be bumped up to 5 stars, and I’ll tell you why.

As many others have mentioned, these chairs aren’t the sturdiest and wobble a bit. The drink holder is placed in an awkward place on the chair (right between your legs) and the chair does take a few minutes to set up, whereas a simple folding chair is done in a few seconds. I imagine this will get better with time, but it does take some elbow grease to get the corners of the chair into the poles. Although the pillow is quite comfortable and really nice, it makes folding the chair a bit more of a pain that the swivel version (because no pillow). One of compaclite’s best features is the fact that…yes…it’s compact, so the pillow adds a stressor that makes it difficult to be easily compact. I struggled for a solid 5 minutes to get this one in the bag.

Ultimately, it comes down to what you value. Do you need something that turns in a circle? Do you want arm rests? Do you want a pillow? Should it be compact? Do you want something that can be easily set up? If you are searching for a compact chair that can easily be carried and don’t mind set-up and break down times, then I would recommend this chair. Otherwise, you might want to look elsewhere if those aren’t your priorities.
text_fidelity_b: Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy I just received the Fitbit One yesterday, so I can't really give as detailed a report as some of the others I've read. I spent a very long time deciding which item to purchase - did I want a Flex? Did I want my heart rate monitored? I think the first thing to figure out is what you exactly want to accomplish.

For my needs, tracking my steps, calories burned and sleep is really what I wanted and the Fitbit One had outstanding ratings. As well, I did not want to have to wear anything on my wrist during the day. The clip vs. band was a huge plus for me. Plus the burgundy color is really nice (though where I clip it, no one sees it anyway).

I downloaded the free Fitbit app and created an account online as soon as I got it (you have to activate and set up online anyway). It asks for your goals as far as weight loss, in what time frame, steps per day goals, etc. You can make changes if you need to. Based on the goals you set for your weight loss amount and how hard you are willing to work for it (from easy at 0.5 lbs/week to very hard at 2 lbs/week), it will calculate how many calories a day you should be eating and then tell you how long it should take to reach your goal. This is the website or app, not the Fitbit One itself.

The Fitbit is small and I barely notice I'm wearing it. The clip is a rubbery material that is very soft, so it is easy to get the One into and out of the clip when you want to put it into the band for sleeping. I clip it to clothes on my upper body as per the instruction recommendations, and I don't remember it is there. You can set a message for when you first start it up, and then you can cycle through various stats, like # steps walked, stairs climbed, miles walked, calories burned, and then it will show the time all on the display.

On the website/app, you will get more details about all the areas that are tracked. When you meet a milestone, it has a little "hooray" for you - for example today I met my steps goal.

If you want it to track your sleep, you need to put it in the sleep band. I did that last night and it is super easy to get the One out of the clip and slip it into the band. I had to keep the band fairly loose so it wouldn't be uncomfortable - it isn't the softest material - but when I fell asleep I didn't even notice I had it on. In the morning, it gave me details about my sleep pattern and how long I was actually sleeping vs. how long I was in bed, which I think is super helpful.

This is a great tool, but like any tool the responsibility is still on the individual. You have to manually enter your food in the online tracker (or in the app), and it will tell you how many calories you've eaten, how many you have left, etc. It will also tell you how many you may have left because of the amount of calories you've burned. But that is all dependent on a person taking the time to put the information in and doing so accurately. For me, that's the hardest part (I've tried food tracker apps in the past). I think once I get into the habit and make it my routine, it shouldn't be so difficult.

Synching data from the One to the computer/app is done wirelessly. I noticed it makes it to my app (via bluetooth) much more quickly than it makes it to my computer. Sometimes I have to refresh the computer several times to get it to show the right number of steps, etc. However, there is so much more information in the online dashboard than in the app, and you can get into great detail about your sleep and other things that I really do want it to synch accurately (and quickly) with my computer.

My one complaint is that I didn't realize it already came with a clip and a sleep band so I bought them separately. That might be MY mistake, though, so I didn't take any stars off for it. But if you want to buy this, unless you want to have an extra clip and band just in case, you do NOT need to buy them separately.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this choice. It was a tough decision but so far so good.

I'll update if status after I've used it for awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Strider Foldable Treadmill, 20-Inch Wide Running Belt with Optional Exclusive SunnyFit™ App and Enhanced Bluetooth Connectivity I should start by saying when I first got this treadmill it was for a Christmas present so I was very happy with it. I am an avid runner and in the winter months I hate being inside without being able to run and a treadmill is a life saver.

When I first started running on the treadmill it was good, although the belt was a little narrow. After about two weeks the motor just randomly stopped while I was running and shut the whole treadmill off.

I spoke to their technical support team and they said I needed to lubricate it which I was doing regularly. I went back and forth with them until finally they sent a new motor. I installed the motor myself of course, and within 2 weeks the same problem was happening.

I decided to tighten the motor a little bit to the belt which ended up helping the issue. At that point I limited my speed on the treadmill in hopes to keep it going, because I still needed to run. After another 2-3 weeks the belt would barely move at highest speeds. I would set it to 7mph and it was at walking speeds.

This continued for a few weeks and then I tightened the motor again. After a month or two of trial and error, tightening motors, etc. the treadmill finally stopped going faster than a walk at all. Today, I just opened the treadmill up and it looks like the motor mounts bent. There is no way to repair it. After all of the headache and trouble, and dealing with not being able to run on long run days, I've decided to give up and purchase a new treadmill from a reputable brand. I would suggest you do the same.

Unfortunately, because I got strung along by their support, I am no longer within my window to get a refund so I guess $600 lost. Please do yourself a favor and find something that will work that is reputable, these off brands suck.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Strider Foldable Treadmill, 20-Inch Wide Running Belt with Optional Exclusive SunnyFit™ App and Enhanced Bluetooth Connectivity

Yukon Charlie's Advanced Spin Snowshoe Kit, Includes Snowshoes, Trekking Poles and Travel Bag I would have loved so much to have these in Utah last month. I did get to try them in some small snow back here on the East coast, which was still cool, but not nearly the same as up in the mountains where the snow has been getting deeper, but also packed down after a season of constant snow.

Wow, this is the next great thing for me, snow-shoeing, when lucky enough to be somewhere to use them well. I love trekking and other outdoor sports, but so many of them take too much "overhead" work or have too much to travel with. These - like a set of fins - fit diagonally in my large checked bag. They take up a lot of room, but at least you don't need an oversized bag to take them along. And it is a lot of fun. You can go so much further - with a real workout, mind you - and fearlessly go further along than the trails without worrying about falling in so often.

It's an all metal frame, and you can wear your favorite hiking boots, and they just tighten round your boots. It's a really nice setup. They also have crampons built in.

Oh, they have a carry bag that comes with it. This is definitely nice to have, but this is probably the only thing that could have really been better, as it is just really thin and won't last super long if at all abused. It could have been made into a backpack or sling bag as well.

They are also the perfect size and fit for me, and aren't too difficult to walk in as I thought they might be. Like I said, definitely a bit of a workout anyway, but that's part of the fun.
